\chapter{Who Governs}

\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say administration, to govern, a minister, a chief minister and a governor.}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഭരണം} (bharaṇaṁ)}{ഭരണം (bharaṇaṁ)}]{\ml{ഭരണം} (bharaṇaṁ) — administration; rule}

\label{lesson:ML-C421-bharanam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a minority, then the Malayalam for to win.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഭരണം}}
\textbf{\ml{ഭരണം}} — \emph{bharaṇaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}administration; rule\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പുതിയ} \ml{ഭരണം} \ml{ജനങ്ങൾക്ക്} \ml{ഇഷ്ടമായി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{putiya bharaṇaṁ janaṅṅaḷkkŭ iṣṭamāyi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The people liked the new administration.
\end{quote}

Under a rule: -\ml{ന്റെ} \ml{ഭരണത്തിൽ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഭരണം}} (\emph{bharaṇaṁ}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{bharaṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}bearing, maintaining\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9395; Monier-Williams), from the root \emph{bhṛ}, \textquotedblleft{}to bear\textquotedblright{}: to rule is to bear the load of a land.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bharaṇaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bharaṇaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{putiya bharaṇaṁ janaṅṅaḷkkŭ iṣṭamāyi.} — The people liked the new administration.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a minority, then the Malayalam for to win, then say \emph{bharaṇaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഭരണം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Administration; rule\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഭരിക്കുക} (bharikkuka)}{ഭരിക്കുക (bharikkuka)}]{\ml{ഭരിക്കുക} (bharikkuka) — to govern; to rule}

\label{lesson:ML-C421-bharikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to win, then the Malayalam for administration.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഭരിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഭരിക്കുക}} — \emph{bharikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to govern; to rule\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ആ} \ml{രാജാവ്} \ml{നാൽപത്} \ml{വർഷം} \ml{നാട്} \ml{ഭരിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā rājāvŭ nālpatŭ varṣaṁ nāṭŭ bhariccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That king ruled the land for forty years.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഭരിച്ചു}, \emph{bhariccu}.

The verb of \ml{ഭരണം}. What is ruled stays unmarked: \ml{നാട്} \ml{ഭരിക്കുക}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഭരിക്കുക}} (\emph{bharikkuka}) is built from the Sanskrit root \emph{bhṛ}, \textquotedblleft{}to bear, to maintain\textquotedblright{}, as in \emph{bharaṇa} (CDIAL 9395), with the Malayalam verb ending -\ml{ിക്കുക}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bharikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bharikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā rājāvŭ nālpatŭ varṣaṁ nāṭŭ bhariccu.} — That king ruled the land for forty years.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to win, then the Malayalam for administration, then say \emph{bharikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഭരിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To govern; to rule\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മന്ത്രി} (mantri)}{മന്ത്രി (mantri)}]{\ml{മന്ത്രി} (mantri) — a minister}

\label{lesson:ML-C421-mantri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for administration, then the Malayalam for to govern.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മന്ത്രി}}
\textbf{\ml{മന്ത്രി}} — \emph{mantri} — \textquotedblleft{}a minister\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മന്ത്രി} \ml{ഇന്ന്} \ml{ഗ്രാമം} \ml{സന്ദർശിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mantri innŭ grāmaṁ sandarśiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The minister visited the village today.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ml{മന്ത്രിമാർ}, \emph{mantrimār}.

Plural: \ml{മന്ത്രിമാർ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മന്ത്രി}} (\emph{mantri}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{mantrin}, \textquotedblleft{}wise, eloquent; a counsellor\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9838), from \emph{mantra}, \textquotedblleft{}counsel\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mantri}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mantri}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mantri innŭ grāmaṁ sandarśiccu.} — The minister visited the village today.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for administration, then the Malayalam for to govern, then say \emph{mantri} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മന്ത്രി} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A minister\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി} (mukhyamantri)}{മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി (mukhyamantri)}]{\ml{മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി} (mukhyamantri) — a chief minister}

\label{lesson:ML-C421-mukhyamantri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to govern, then the Malayalam for a minister.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി}}
\textbf{\ml{മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി}} — \emph{mukhyamantri} — \textquotedblleft{}a chief minister\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി} \ml{പുതിയ} \ml{ആശുപത്രി} \ml{തുറന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mukhyamantri putiya āśupatri tuṟannu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The chief minister opened the new hospital.
\end{quote}

\ml{മുഖ്യ}-, chief, also makes \ml{മുഖ്യ} \ml{കാരണം}, the main reason.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി}} (\emph{mukhyamantri}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{mukhya}, \textquotedblleft{}of the face; chief\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10174), and \emph{mantrin}, \textquotedblleft{}a counsellor\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9838).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mukhyamantri}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mukhyamantri}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mukhyamantri putiya āśupatri tuṟannu.} — The chief minister opened the new hospital.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to govern, then the Malayalam for a minister, then say \emph{mukhyamantri} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മുഖ്യമന്ത്രി} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A chief minister\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഗവർണർ} (gavarṇar)}{ഗവർണർ (gavarṇar)}]{\ml{ഗവർണർ} (gavarṇar) — a governor}

\label{lesson:ML-C421-gavarnar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a minister, then the Malayalam for a chief minister.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഗവർണർ}}
\textbf{\ml{ഗവർണർ}} — \emph{gavarṇar} — \textquotedblleft{}a governor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഗവർണർ} \ml{ഇന്നലെ} \ml{നഗരത്തിൽ} \ml{എത്തി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gavarṇar innale nagarattil etti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The governor reached the city yesterday.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ml{ഗവർണർമാർ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഗവർണർ}} (\emph{gavarṇar}) was borrowed from English \emph{governor}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gavarṇar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gavarṇar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gavarṇar innale nagarattil etti.} — The governor reached the city yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a minister, then the Malayalam for a chief minister, then say \emph{gavarṇar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഗവർണർ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A governor\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
